content.user_title: Build CloudBase Relational Database Web Clients
content.value_statement: Browser apps need a clear CloudBase relational database setup path. This skill shows the shared web SDK client and Supabase-style query flow.
actual_capabilities: Identifies when browser apps should use the CloudBase relational database web SDK.
Shows the package needed for @cloudbase/js-sdk setup.
Defines one shared CloudBase app and relational database client pattern.
Explains that authentication should be handled before table access.
Routes schema management, MCP operations, backend access, and PostgreSQL tasks to other skills.
Provides Supabase-style select, insert, update, and delete examples.
limitations: Does not provision MySQL instances or modify schemas.
Does not cover backend Node service access.
Does not replace CloudBase authentication setup.
Assumes the browser app can use @cloudbase/js-sdk.

use_cases.title: Create a Shared Web Client
use_cases.description: Set up one CloudBase app and relational database client for a frontend project.

use_cases.title: Migrate Browser Queries
use_cases.description: Move Supabase-style browser table queries into CloudBase relational database patterns.

use_cases.title: Route Database Tasks
use_cases.description: Separate browser data access from schema management, MCP operations, backend access, and PostgreSQL work.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the basic CloudBase relational database setup for a browser app.

prompt_templates.title: Shared Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a shared frontend database client using @cloudbase/js-sdk and explain where auth belongs.

prompt_templates.title: Supabase Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Supabase browser query migration to CloudBase relational database patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Architecture Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my frontend data access plan and separate browser queries from MCP schema management.

output_examples.input: Build a shared database client for a Vue app.
output_examples.output: A concise setup plan naming the shared CloudBase app, auth step, and relational database client.

output_examples.input: Migrate Supabase list queries to CloudBase.
output: Query behavior notes for browser table reads.
Warnings about keeping schema work outside frontend code.

output_examples.input: Decide whether a task belongs in this skill.
output_examples.output: A routing answer that sends browser queries here and sends MySQL administration or PostgreSQL work to the right skill.

best_practices: Create one shared frontend database client and reuse it across components.
Handle authentication before relational table access.
Keep schema changes and privileged administration outside browser code.
anti_patterns: Do not initialize CloudBase inside every component.
Do not use this skill for MCP database management.
Do not mix PostgreSQL semantics with the CloudBase web relational flow.

faq.question: Can this skill create database tables?
faq.answer: No. It routes schema and provisioning work to relational-database-tool or PostgreSQL guidance.

faq.question: Is it for backend services?
faq.answer: No. It is for browser apps that use @cloudbase/js-sdk.

faq.question: Does it include authentication flows?
faq.answer: It notes that auth must be handled separately before data access.

faq.question: Can it help Supabase migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps browser client setup and query patterns to CloudBase relational database usage.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents an install command and client patterns. Users or agents decide what to execute.
